title: Catalyst onboarding session plan and slide skeleton
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a facilitator-first session plan and a compact slide skeleton for a 3-hour Catalyst onboarding workshop with Acme Retail (POC kickoff). Goal: align technical stakeholders, validate the target inference topology, collect performance targets and dataset/prompt surface, and produce a crisp next-step deployment proposal (Dedicated vs Hosted + fallback plan).

High-level goals:
- Shared understanding of success criteria (latency P95, throughput, cost target per 1M tokens).
- Confirm data security and network requirements (VPC, SSO, KMS).
- Run a short end-to-end demo of a representative prompt set and agree on evaluation harness.
- Capture rollout plan: pilot -> scale -> SLA requirements.

Prework for customer (sent 1 week in advance):
- Provide 10 representative prompts + expected outputs (CSV).
- IP/data classification form (simple checklist) to decide hosted vs private.
content_addendum:
NOTE: some Drive docs here are kept minimal and iterative; this file is intentionally conversational. Below: timeboxed agenda, slide skeleton, facilitation scripts, risk log, and follow-ups.

Agenda (3 hours)
- 0:00–0:10 — Welcome + introductions (facilitator: Maya)
  - Quick round: role, success measure for this POC (1 sentence each).
- 0:10–0:25 — Goals & success criteria (workshop)
  - Live edit of Success Criteria doc (Confluence link). Capture numeric targets.
- 0:25–0:40 — Architecture primer (Redwood serving modes)
  - One slide: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (decision matrix).
- 0:40–1:10 — Customer topology & constraints (customer engineers present)
  - Map network, data residency, auth. Whiteboard required.
- 1:10–1:30 — Demo: representative prompt run (engineer-run)
  - Show latency, token counts, and sample outputs.
- 1:30–1:45 — Breakout #1: failure modes & mitigation (small groups)
  - Each group lists 3 failure modes and quick mitigations.
- 1:45–2:10 — Quant & perf targets / batching strategy
  - Present batching/kv-cache options and cost tradeoffs.
- 2:10–2:40 — Deployment options exercise: map pilot plan
  - Decide Dedicated vs Hosted pilot, autoscale policy, rollback triggers.
- 2:40–2:55 — Acceptance criteria & evaluation harness (who runs tests)
- 2:55–3:00 — Next steps, owners, and close

Slide skeleton (10–12 slides)
1) Title + participants + date + POC overview (one-liner objective)
2) Agenda & desired outcomes
3) Success criteria (metric table) – ask customer to confirm live
4) Where Redwood fits: brief bullet on runtime, caching, smart routing
5) Decision matrix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (security, latency, cost)
6) Customer topology (diagram) — network, data flow, ingress points
7) Demo snapshots: token distribution, sample outputs, latency histogram
8) Cost & performance levers: batching, quantization, model variants
9) Pilot rollforward plan: phases, timeline, KPIs, rollback criteria
10) Evaluation harness: acceptance test list, owners, schedule
11) Risks & open questions (live notes)
12) Action items & owners (next 30/60/90 days)

Facilitation notes & scripts (bite-sized prompts)
- Opening: "We want to leave here with one clear next-step: pilot type and three owners. If we don't pick a pilot today, we will at least have a clear blockers list and decision timeline."
- When discussing success criteria: ask each stakeholder to name the single metric that will make them call the POC a success. Write these verbatim.
- Demo run: ask customer to run the representative prompt so we capture realistic tokenization. If they cannot, run our synthetic but flag differences.
- Breakouts: keep groups to 3–4 people; give them a single sticky note each to submit top 3 risks. Collect and cluster.

Templates & quick checklists to capture during session
- Network checklist: egress ports, private endpoints, firewall rules, IP allowlist, KMS access? (Y/N)
- Data access: Does the model see raw PII? (Y/N). If Y -> mark for Private deployment discussion.
- Latency target table: P50, P95, P99, expected concurrency, max token length.

Risk register (starter items to update live)
- Data residency unclear -> potential blocker for Hosted. Mitigation: propose Dedicated in customer VPC or Private instance.
- Unknown prompt distribution -> run mini-load test with 1k queries. Owner: Jordan. Due: +7 days.
- Integration auth complexity (SSO / SCIM) -> solutions-engineering to scope SSO flow. Owner: Ravi.

Acceptance tests (short list)
- Output correctness: 200 sample prompts produce >= 90% pass rate vs golden answers (owner: customer QA).
- Latency: P95 under target for 95% of runs at pilot concurrency (owner: SRE/Redwood).
- Security: no outbound data leakage in staged tests (owner: security).

Post-workshop deliverables (within 5 business days)
- One-page pilot recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) with estimated cost per million tokens. Owner: Maya.
- Deployment runbook draft (network steps, firewall rules, preflight checklist). Owner: Ravi.
- Evaluation harness repo (simple scripts + sample dataset). Owner: Jordan.
- Updated Confluence page and Jira epic with tasks and owners.

Facilitator tips (practical)
- Keep momentum: if a discussion is taking > 10 minutes, park and move to action item.
- Use live editing in Confluence during the session so stakeholders can see final language.
- Record the session (with permission) for follow-up and to extract demo traces.

Open questions to resolve after session
- Can Acme provide a small (anonymized) dataset for template tuning?
- Are there regulatory reviews required for production deployment? Who owns them?

Appendix: Quick technical notes (rapid reference)
- Batching implications: higher batch size reduces cost per token but increases P95 latency; suggest adaptive batching with latency SLO ceilings.
- KV cache: effective when repetition/prefix reuse is high; bring representative chat traces to evaluate.
- Quantization: 4-bit quant reduces memory and cost but verify quality on golden prompts.

End-of-doc checklist (for facilitator to complete within 48h)
- Upload action items to Jira and tag owners (SE-9872).
- Share slide deck draft with customer and request confirmation of success criteria.
- Schedule technical deep-dive for infra team if Dedicated/Private chosen.

(Inline links used during session)
- Confluence draft: confluence:SE-CATALYST-ONBOARD-234
- Jira epic: SE-9872
- Slack channel: #se-catalyst-acme

Notes about tone: keep verbal language concise and avoid deep academic framing in the initial workshop — customers appreciate concrete, measurable outcomes.

-- End of facilitator session plan --
